study_identification_part.si4_title: Neuroanatomical heterogeneity and homogeneity in individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its objectives: to quantify neuroanatomical heterogeneity in CHR-P individuals compared to healthy controls and in relation to psychosis transition, and to use a normative modeling approach (PBSI) to assess 'normativeness'.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text:
We aimed to quantify the neuroanatomical heterogeneity in structural magnetic resonance imaging measures of cortical surface area (SA), cortical thickness (CT), subcortical volume (SV), and intracranial volume (ICV) in CHR-P individuals compared with healthy controls (HC), and in relation to subsequent transition to a first episode of psychosis.
...using a normative modelling approach, to assess the ' normativeness ' of neuroanatomical profiles in individuals at CHR-P.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study uses the ENIGMA CHR-P dataset. It cites the original publication for participant inclusion/exclusion criteria. It specifies image quality standards (outliers, visual inspection, missing ROIs exclusion) and reports the final sample size (1243 HC).
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: The ENIGMA CHR-P dataset amalgamated clinical and neuroimaging data from 29 sites... Further participant inclusion and exclusion criteria have been previously described [20]... The ENIGMA quality control procedure identifies outliers (±2 SD from the mean) and includes a visual inspection of all images... Participants with >5% missing ROIs were excluded... final sample consisted of... 1243 HC participants
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.location: Methods/Participants; Methods/MRI data acquisition and processing; Results/Sample characteristics

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Covariates like age and sex are controlled for. Site effects are addressed using neuroComBat.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text:
Neuroimaging data were adjusted for scanner protocol and site using neuroComBat [50]... controlling for group (CHR-P/HC), age and sex.
All multivariable regression models were applied, adjusting for age and sex.

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The Person-Based Similarity Index (PBSI) calculation inherently uses a leave-one-out strategy, correlating each individual with all other members of the group (j != i).
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: The PBSI of the ith individual is the average correlation between his/her brain measures ( yi ) and the brain measures of any other individual of the reference sample ( yj , for j ≠ i ).

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study analyzes a single pooled dataset (ENIGMA CHR-P) and does not report applying the model to an independent external dataset of healthy individuals not included in the pooled analysis.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: The ENIGMA CHR-P consortium applied a harmonised analysis to neuroimaging data across 29 sites, including 1579 CHR-P individuals and 1243 HC, offering the largest pooled CHR-P neuroimaging dataset to date.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach (Person-Based Similarity Index, using Spearman correlations) is described. Software availability (R code) is stated.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: Personalised estimates of heterogeneity... indexed with the novel Person-Based Similarity Index (PBSI)... using a normative modelling approach... Within each group, and for each brain phenotype, Spearman correlation coefficients were computed... Computer code to calculate the VR, CVR and PBSI statistics is available from the authors upon request.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.location: Abstract; Methods/Person-Based Similarity Index; CODE AVAILABILITY

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: While the study establishes a normative reference using PBSI and reports the distribution of scores, it does not explicitly report quantitative metrics of model fit or calibration (like explained variance or prediction error) for the reference cohort itself, which is a standard requirement for normative models.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: The respective neuroanatomical profiles of each CHR-P individual were correlated with the corresponding profiles of the members of the HC group, for each brain phenotype. The resulting PBSI scores thus represent the degree of deviation from the ' normative ' range and were transformed into z -scores

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: The study uses a Leave-One-Out strategy (inherent in PBSI), meaning there are no distinct 'partitions' (like training/test folds) with separate characteristics to report. The characteristics of the full cohort are reported.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: The PBSI of the ith individual is the average correlation between his/her brain measures ( yi ) and the brain measures of any other individual of the reference sample ( yj , for j ≠ i ).
